subject: IAM evidence request and SOC 2 status - Redwood / Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lara Chen <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: IAM evidence request and SOC 2 status - Redwood / Acme Health

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo and for walking through Acme Health's use case today — appreciate the time. As discussed on the call, security/compliance is the primary track for procurement. To keep momentum on the vendor review I wanted to summarize next steps on IAM and SOC 2 evidence so your security team has a clear checklist.

High-level asks (we can iterate):
- SOC 2: current attestations (type II preferred), date, and a copy or secure link to the report.
- SSO: IdP metadata (SAML metadata XML) or OIDC issuer + discovery endpoint.
- SCIM: provisioning endpoint/base URL, schema attributes supported (userName, givenName, familyName, emails, groups), and any rate limits.
- RBAC/admin controls: description of admin roles, who can invite/remove users, and any approval/workflow for privilege escalation.
- Evidence uploads: if easier, we can accept artifacts in your security portal or via a secure Drive link / DocuSign.

If you prefer, we can kick off our vendor security questionnaire (I can send the questionnaire link and you can complete or upload answers). Target timeline from Acme to avoid slowing procurement would be: SOC 2 + SSO metadata within 3 business days, SCIM details within 1 week. Is that feasible?

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (high-level), SSO-setup-guide.pdf (our SSO/SP setup example).

Next steps:
- Jordan: share SOC 2 link and SAML metadata / OIDC endpoints.
- Lara (cc): security contact to receive questionnaire or upload artifacts.
- Marissa: will follow up and loop in Redwood security (Aditya) and solutions (Dylan) for technical review.

Thanks — speak soon.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary and for the call today. We can definitely start moving this forward. Per your asks: 

- SOC 2: We completed a SOC 2 Type II for 2026. The auditor report is available in our security portal; sharing here: https://acmehealth-secure.com/reports/soc2-2026 (internal link, access granted to security@redwood.com).
- SSO: Attaching our SAML metadata XML (acme-idp-metadata.xml) to this reply and including our SP configuration notes. We also expose OIDC discovery at https://idp.acmehealth.com/.
- SCIM: Provisioning API base: https://api.acmehealth.com/scim/v2. Supported attributes: userName, givenName, familyName, email, active, groups. We will provide a formal schema doc and rate-limit details tomorrow.
- RBAC/admin: Our admin role model is documented in the linked security portal page. Admins are managed by the IAM team with approvals required for privileged role changes.

I'll begin the vendor questionnaire now and aim to have the bulk of artifacts uploaded to the portal by end of day tomorrow. If Redwood's security team wants to review the SAML metadata or run a quick test, let us know preferred SP ACS and EntityID and we can coordinate.

Attaching: acme_soc2_report_2026.pdf (redacted), acme-idp-metadata.xml

Folks — forwarding Acme's reply. They provided a SOC 2 link and SAML metadata; attaching the PDF they sent. Can you review and advise on the technical asks below? Quick asks from me: 

1) Can we accept their SAML metadata as-is? Any SP config notes we should send back (ACS/EntityID)?
2) SCIM: confirm attribute mapping for provisioning (we usually need email, externalId, and groups). Any special mapping or custom attributes needed?
3) RBAC/admin: Aditya, please confirm our minimum evidence for admin controls and what we should require in the questionnaire (e.g., admin audit logs, user deprovisioning SLA).

Timing: procurement wants SOC 2 + SSO metadata within 3 business days. If we can validate quickly we'll stay on track for their POC next month.

Thanks — I'll coordinate a short tech check call if you want to run the SAML metadata against a test SP.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Thanks — quick internal checklist from security: 

- SAML metadata: we can accept XML. Please confirm ACS URL and EntityID we will use for Redwood test SP: https://api.redwood.com/saml/acs and EntityID: https://redwood.com/saml/metadata. We'll provide sample SP metadata back to them.
- OIDC: if they have OIDC available that's fine; we prefer OIDC for provisioning but SAML is ok for SSO.
- SCIM: confirm they support groups and that PATCH is allowed. Request their SCIM base + test credentials; we'll run a sandbox provisioning test. Required attributes: userName, externalId, emails, active, groups.
- RBAC/admin evidence: request admin role definitions, list of current admins, and sample audit logs showing invite/removal events (last 90 days). Also ask for user deprovisioning SLA/process.

I'll start filling the vendor questionnaire with the above asks and set a 48hr deadline for initial evidence. Dylan — can you validate whether any custom SCIM attributes are needed for our product (e.g., team_id)? If yes, flag and I'll add to the questionnaire.

Aditya
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
